source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
For a durian tree that has already begun bearing fruit, this source gives two more nutrient programs.

After pruning post-harvest: broadcast compost/manure at 15-50kg per tree (about 3-10 baskets) plus chemical fertilizer 15-15-15 or 16-16-16 at 3-5kg per tree, worked into the soil under the canopy drip-line.

When the tree has no flowers yet: apply fertilizer 8-24-24, 9-24-24, or 17-24-12 (all relatively low-nitrogen, phosphorus/potassium-forward formulas meant to encourage flower bud formation rather than vegetative leaf growth) at 2-3kg per tree, worked into the soil, to help push the tree toward flowering.

General cautions from the source: keep grass and weeds cleared from under the canopy before fertilizing so nutrients are not lost to weed competition; water in fertilizer within 10-14 days of application, in moderate amounts, so the tree can take it up gradually -- do not flood-irrigate immediately after fertilizing, since heavy water directly after application can wash nutrients away and burn surface roots; and be careful applying fertilizer close to flowering time, since excess nitrogen at that stage can cause flowers to abort.
